commands.author: FMLS

target.title: feat(browser): add `openclaw browser batch` CLI subcommand
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The browser runtime already supports `act:batch` (nested `actions[]` in one
`/act` call), but the CLI surface had no `batch` subcommand: a user or script
on the CLI could only run one action per `openclaw browser <action>` invocation,
so batching was reachable solely through the agent tool / HTTP route. M1.6 of
the browser tool plan closes that gap by exposing `openclaw browser batch` and
finalizing the batch semantics (ref lifecycle, target id conflicts, error
summary) in docs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Batch CLI/semantics finalization (M1.6 in the browser tool plan), scoped to
CLI exposure + docs; no runtime behavior change.

- Add `openclaw browser batch` subcommand that builds a `kind: "batch"` body
  from nested act requests and posts it to the existing `/act` route.
- `--actions <json>` for inline JSON, `--actions-file <path>` for file input,
  `--actions-file -` for stdin. `readActionsPayload` (shared.ts:151) picks the
  source; `readStdinText` (shared.ts:133) caps stdin at 1MB
  (`ACTIONS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`, shared.ts:130) so a runaway pipe cannot fill
  memory.
- `--continue` sets `stopOnError=false`. Default omits `stopOnError` so the
  route applies its existing fail-fast default (stop on first error), matching
  the batch contract. There is no `--bail` flag because bail is the default.
- `--target-id` forwards to the batch body (same `BROWSER_TAB_REFERENCE_HELP`
  as sibling action commands).
- Outer request timeout uses `resolveBrowserActExecutionBudgetMs` so the
  batch budget covers nested actions (same path the node proxy uses for
  batch sizing).
- Docs (`docs/tools/browser-control.md` + bundled `browser-automation` skill)
  add a "Browser batch CLI" section documenting the CLI, ref lifecycle inside
  `actions[]`, `targetId` conflict handling, and the error summary format
  returned for `stopOnError=false`.

## User Impact

CLI users and scripts can now run a batch of browser actions in one call
(`openclaw browser batch --actions '[...]'` or `--actions-file -` from a
pipe), removing per-action round trips. The default fail-fast behavior is
unchanged; `--continue` is opt-in for running through all actions. No
runtime, config, or existing CLI flag changes; users who do not use the new
subcommand are unaffected.

## Evidence

HEAD: `b5b8e7c118771077f65a6d089597ed4e6f34e622`
Branch: `feat/browser-batch-cli` (fork: FMLS/openclaw), rebased onto
`upstream/main` (`6dc6d5efeeb`); diff contains only the 8 M1.6 files below.

### Live terminal capture (HEAD b5b8e7c1187)

Focused test for the new surface (`register.batch.ts` + `shared.ts`
`readActionsPayload`), verbose reporter. All 10 cases pass:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-input/register.batch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > sends normalized batch body with inline actions and target id 19ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > omits stopOnError by default so the route applies its fail-fast default 2ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > sets stopOnError=false when --continue is passed 1ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > reads actions from a file via --actions-file 2ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > reads actions from stdin when --actions-file is - 1ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > rejects malformed actions JSON before dispatch 3ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > rejects non-array actions before dispatch 1ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > rejects empty actions before dispatch 1ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > requires actions from --actions, --actions-file, or stdin 2ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| .../register.batch.test.ts > browser action input batch command > budgets the outer request from the batch execution budget 1ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
   Duration  8.64s (transform 4.51s, setup 326ms, import 8.06s, tests 42ms)
```

### Whole-surface inspection

- Shared implementation: `register.batch.ts:22-77` builds the `kind: "batch"`
  body, validates JSON/array/non-empty, and posts via `callBrowserAct`.
  `shared.ts:151-159` (`readActionsPayload`) selects inline/file/stdin;
  `shared.ts:130-148` (`readStdinText` + 1MB cap) bounds stdin.
- Entry points: `register.ts` calls `registerBrowserBatchCommands(browser,
  parentOpts)` next to the sibling action-input registrars;
  `browser-cli.ts` lists `batch` in the lazy `placeholders` array so the
  subcommand resolves without eager-loading the actions-input module;
  `browser-cli-examples.ts` adds a batch example for `--help`.
- Sibling surfaces (share the invariant "one `kind` body -> `/act` route,
  timeout from `resolveBrowserActExecutionBudgetMs`"): `register.navigation.ts`,
  `register.element.ts`, `register.form-wait-eval.ts`, `register.files-downloads.ts`.
  `batch` reuses the same `callBrowserAct` + `resolveBrowserActionContext` +
  `BROWSER_TAB_REFERENCE_HELP` helpers, so it inherits the same timeout-slack
  and profile-routing behavior; no new routing path.
- Sibling tests: `register.navigation.test.ts`, `register.element.test.ts`,
  `register.form-wait-eval.test.ts`, `register.files-downloads.test.ts`,
  `shared.test.ts`. New `register.batch.test.ts` mirrors their structure
  (spy on `callBrowserRequest` + `readActionsPayload`, assert body shape and
  pre-dispatch validation) and adds the batch-specific `stopOnError`-default
  and execution-budget assertions.
- Feature history: the runtime batch path (`BROWSER_ACT_KINDS` includes
  `batch`, `resolveBrowserActExecutionBudgetMs` sizes nested actions) is
  already shipped and covered by `browser-tool.test.ts` (batch sizing, stale
  target recovery). M1.6 adds CLI exposure + docs only; no runtime change.

### Static checks

- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`: clean (no whitespace errors).
- `tsgo:extensions`: typecheck pass for `extensions/browser` (run locally).
- `oxlint` (`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the changed files): pass.
- `oxfmt --check` on changed `.ts` + `.md` files: pass.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs .../register.batch.test.ts --reporter=verbose`:
  10/10 pass (capture above).

### Notes

- `autoreview` was opted out for this PR: the local environment has no
  `codex` / `claude` / `pi` CLI, so the autoreview skill cannot run locally.
  All other local checks (format, tsgo, lint, focused tests, `git diff
  --check`) are green.
- This PR is independent of M0.2 (#111381): it was rebased onto
  `upstream/main` with the M0.2 commit dropped, so the diff shows only the
  M1.6-specific files (8 files, +358/-1). The "Browser batch CLI" docs
  section is self-contained (includes a one-line batch intro) so it reads
  correctly on `main` even before #111381 lands; if #111381 merges first,
  its "Act kinds and batch" section and this section can be reconciled in a
  follow-up to avoid duplicated batch intro text.
